findings.title: Apply the finite runtime budget to Docker inspection and preserve owned cleanup on outer timeout
findings.evidence: qualify_runtime.py declares a 600s outer budget but calls image inspection outside execute() with no subprocess timeout. run_runtime.py bounds only docker wait; create/start/inspect/log/stop/rm have no timeout. The parent executes this launcher with timeout remaining-10 and subprocess.run kills the launcher on TimeoutExpired rather than invoking its finally block. The parent has no container cleanup fallback; create is also outside the launcher's try block. A stalled inspection can exceed the outer bound, while a stalled Docker command after creation can leave the owned container present or running after the launcher is killed.
findings.required_change: Bound every Docker subprocess against an absolute deadline; reserve a finite cleanup budget, record owned container identity before potentially blocking creation, and guarantee coordinator-owned cleanup if the launcher times out. Keep failed qualification/evidence visible and never mark removal/inspection as successful when unobserved.
findings.validation: Coordinator should exercise a deterministic Docker-command timeout after container creation and verify finite failure, saved FAIL receipt and cleanup of only the owned container; also verify image-inspection timeout. Reviewer did not execute a mock/runtime.
